les: Gr 4 Sosiale Wetenskappe: gedeelde woordelysomskrywings (stel 2026-10-07, 37 inskrywings)
kaps_punt: nvt: gedeelde woordelysstel, nie een KAPS-punt nie

items.bewering: 'n Verkleinde tekening wat van bo af wys waar dinge in 'n plek lê.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Map' (education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/map): a map is a symbolic representation of a place, usually drawn on a flat surface, at a reduced scale; maps are drawn from a bird's-eye (plan) view.

items.bewering: Plante wat mense kweek vir kos en vir ander produkte.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Crops' (education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/crops): crops are plants or plant products grown to provide food, fuel, clothing and more; FAO AGROVOC c_1972: plants cultivated for food, fibre, fodder or other uses.

items.bewering: Boerdery waar diere aangehou word vir die produkte wat ons van hulle kry.
items.bron: New World Encyclopedia, 'Livestock': domesticated animals raised in an agricultural setting to produce products such as meat, eggs, milk, fur, leather and wool (and also to provide labour, e.g. draught oxen, which the definition omits without falsifying anything).

items.bewering: Water wat baie min sout bevat, soos die water in riviere en mere.
items.bron: USGS water-use reports (usgs.gov, 'Surface water use'): water with less than 1 000 mg/L dissolved solids is freshwater. Rivers and lakes are the standard examples. NOTE: National Geographic Education 'Lake' confirms closed lakes are typically saline (Great Salt Lake); 'die water in mere' is a typical example, not true of every lake. Passed because 'soos' introduces examples, but see the set item on meer/varswater.

items.bewering: 'n Groot opgaartenk waar skoon water gestoor word voordat dit na mense versprei word.
items.bron: Engineering News 2023-03-03 and 2024-04-05 on Rand Water: treated potable water is stored in bulk storage reservoirs and pumped to municipal reservoirs before reaching consumers; Afrikaans municipal usage 'reservoirvlakke' (suidkaapforum.com, Heidelberg en Slangrivier, 2023-11-28); DWS 25 ML 'Command Reservoir', Moretele (dws.gov.za, 2025). NOTE: internationally, and in some older South African names (the Table Mountain 'reservoirs'), the word also means a dam lake of untreated water; the definition gives the current everyday South African municipal sense only. Not false, and it keeps reservoir and opgaardam distinct in the set.

items.bewering: 'n Groot hoeveelheid water wat vanself gevorm het en deur land omring word.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Lake' (education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/lake): 'People make lakes by digging basins or by damming rivers or springs. These artificial lakes can become reservoirs' (Lake Mead, behind the Hoover Dam). Lake Kariba (Afrikaans 'Karibameer') on the Zambezi is man-made, formed behind a dam wall built 1955-1959 (zambiatourism.com, Lake Kariba history; zimfieldguide.com, Kariba Dam construction).
items.regstelling: FOUT (vals 'net'): 'wat vanself gevorm het' is given as a defining feature, so the entry says every lake formed by itself. Reference sources count man-made lakes as lakes, and a well-known southern African one (Karibameer) was made behind a dam wall. The contrast with 'dam' can stay; the fault is the absolute. The writer should narrow the quantifier (most lakes / usually) rather than state natural origin as part of what a lake is. No replacement wording proposed here.

items.bewering: Water wat mense agter 'n damwal opgaar wat hulle self gebou het.
items.bron: Dictionary of South African English, 'dam' (dsae.co.za/entry/dam/e01904): in South Africa 'dam' denotes the body of water (a man-made pond or reservoir where water is collected for storage), and 'wal' takes the place of the Dutch 'dam' for the wall. WEET, 'Damme van Suid-Afrika' (weet.co.za/skoolwerk/damme-van-suid-afrika): ''n Dam se definisie is 'n plek waar water opgegaar word'; damwal: ''n Muur wat in 'n rivier gebou word om water op te dam'.

items.bewering: 'n Diep gat wat met masjiene in die grond geboor word tot by ondergrondse water. Gewoonlik bring 'n pomp die water na bo.
items.bron: DWS groundwater report (dws.gov.za/ghreport/reports/2.2(3306).pdf) and South African borehole-siting/drilling summaries: boreholes are machine-drilled (percussion drilling), typically 36-120 m deep, and pump-tested; UWC thesis on Table Mountain Group artesian aquifers (etd.uwc.ac.za/handle/11394/4369): dozens of flowing artesian boreholes overflow without a pump, which is why 'gewoonlik' is correct and must stay.

items.bewering: Die gemiddelde weerstoestande in 'n gebied oor 'n lang tydperk, soos die temperatuur en die hoeveelheid reën.
items.bron: WMO: climate is average weather over a long period, classically 30 years; climate normals are 30-year averages of elements such as temperature and precipitation (Swiss National Centre for Climate Services, 'What is climate', nccs.admin.ch, citing WMO).

items.bewering: Iets wat mense maklik raaksien en help om 'n plek te herken of te vind.
items.bron: WEET, 'Baken' (weet.co.za/skoolwerk/baken): a baken or landmerk is an easily recognisable object that stands out in the environment, natural or man-made, used to find one's way and determine position. Afrikaans 'baken' also means a survey beacon (DSAE 'beacon'); the landmark sense given is correct.

items.bewering: Hoe iets lyk wanneer 'n mens reguit van bo af daarop neerkyk.
items.bron: Dictionary.com 'plan view': a drawing of something as seen from above / the top view; National Geographic Education 'Map': maps are drawn from a bird's-eye perspective. 'Reguit van bo af' correctly excludes an oblique view.

items.bewering: 'n Plek wat mense of diere veilig hou en teen wind, reën, koue en hitte beskerm.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries / Merriam-Webster Learner's 'shelter': a structure or place that keeps people or animals safe from bad weather or danger. The list of four weathers is read as the range of what shelter protects against, not a test every shelter must pass.

items.bewering: Iets wat mense nodig het om veilig en gesond te leef.
items.bron: Basic needs are things necessary to sustain life and physical/mental well-being: food, water, clothing, shelter, plus safe water, sanitation, health (definitions.uslegal.com 'Basic needs'; lawinsider 'basic needs'). Consistent with the needs-versus-wants distinction.

items.bewering: Iets uit die natuur wat mense gebruik om in hulle behoeftes te voorsien.
items.bron: Natural resources are 'materials from the Earth that are used to support life and meet people's needs' (National Geographic Education wording, reproduced in geoversity.io 'Earth resources'; the NatGeo page itself returned 404). NOTE on the set: read strictly with 'behoefte' (needs = to live safely and healthily), gold or diamonds used for jewellery would fall outside; NatGeo uses the same 'needs' wording, so not treated as a fault.

items.bewering: Om gewasse met water nat te lei wanneer daar te min reën val.
items.bron: FAO AGROVOC c_3954 'irrigation': controlled application of water to agricultural land to allow the cultivation of crops where otherwise, owing to a deficiency of rainfall, agriculture would be impossible; UN-ESCWA glossary: artificial application of water to assist the growing of crops (and pastures).

items.bewering: 'n Lys op 'n kaart wat verduidelik wat die simbole daarop beteken.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Map': every map includes 'a legend or key, which offers not only the bar scale of the map, but also a list of symbols and what they represent'.

items.bewering: Dit wat dinge laat werk, laat beweeg of laat lig gee.
items.bron: US EIA, 'What is energy?' (eia.gov/energyexplained/what-is-energy): 'Scientists define energy as the ability to do work'; energy appears as motion, light, heat. The entry is a Grade 4 functional definition of the same idea. NOTE: electricity also fits the wording, but electricity is a form of energy, so the fit is a subset, not a rival meaning.

items.bewering: Een van die sewe baie groot dele van die aarde se land.
items.bron: New World Encyclopedia 'Continents': 'By convention there are seven continents'; five- and six-continent models also exist (Mental Floss / Cognito 'How many continents are there'). Seven is the convention in South African map work (Oxford Primary Atlas for South Africa, CAPS-aligned; product description only, not opened). A convention, stated as one.

items.bewering: Een van die vyf baie groot waterruimtes om die kontinente.
items.bron: US Board on Geographic Names approved 'Southern Ocean' in 1999; NOAA recognised it; National Geographic recognised five oceans on 8 June 2021 (Polarjournal 2021-06-23; Boston Globe 2021-06-11). NOTE: the International Hydrographic Organization's 2000 draft including the Southern Ocean was never ratified, so 'five' is the current common convention, like 'seven' continents.

items.bewering: 'n Stuk land met water aan alle kante, kleiner as die kleinste kontinent.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Island': 'An island is a body of land surrounded by water'; continents are also surrounded by water but are not islands because of their size; Australia, the smallest continent, is more than three times the size of Greenland, the largest island; islands also occur in rivers. Superlative 'kleinste kontinent' (Australia) holds under the seven-continent convention used in the set.

items.bewering: 'n Letter en 'n nommer wat saam een blokkie op 'n kaart noem.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Map': simple grids use lettered columns and numbered rows for location reference (like 'D7'); alphanumeric (atlas) grid: each cell identified by a letter and a number. NOTE: purely numeric grid references (eastings/northings) also exist; the entry describes the alphanumeric grid used at this grade and is not false there, but it would need widening in a later grade.

items.bewering: Om plante te kweek en diere aan te hou vir kos en ander produkte.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries 'farming': producing food, milk, wool or other products by keeping animals or growing plants. NOTE: the source says 'or'; the entry says 'en'. Read as the range of the activity (as 'kos en ander produkte' in the same sentence is), it is true; read as a requirement, a crop-only farm would not be 'boerdery'. Passed, flagged for the person.

items.bewering: Die reis van water wat oor en oor verdamp, wolke vorm, as reën val en weer wegvloei.
items.bron: USGS Water Science School, 'Evaporation and the water cycle' and water-cycle diagrams: evaporation, condensation into clouds, precipitation, runoff, repeating. Simplifications (snow/hail, soaking into the ground, plant transpiration omitted) are omissions, not false claims. Analogy 'reis': mapping holds - the same water moves from place to place and 'oor en oor' supplies the repetition, so a learner is not led to think water is used up or created; the entry does not say where the journey starts, so the earlier 'starts at the sea' fault is absent.

items.bewering: Wanneer water in waterdamp verander en in die lug opstyg.
items.bron: USGS Water Science School, 'Evaporation and the water cycle': evaporation is the process that changes liquid water to gaseous water (water vapour), moving water from the surface to the atmosphere; WEET 'Watersiklus': water 'in waterdamp oorgaan'.

items.bewering: Water in die lug in 'n vorm wat jy nie kan sien nie.
items.bron: NASA Science for Kids, 'How do clouds form?' (science.nasa.gov/kids/earth/how-do-clouds-form): water vapour is an invisible gas; clouds form when it turns into liquid droplets. Visible 'steam' is condensed droplets, not vapour.

items.bewering: Wanneer water van die land af weer terug na die see vloei.
items.bron: TRIED, and could not settle: Afrikaans searches for 'invloei' with watersiklus / afloop / verdamping / see; WEET 'Watersiklus' (weet.co.za/skoolwerk/watersiklus) names this stage 'oppervlakwater' that 'bogronds terugvloei see toe' and uses 'insypel' for water entering the ground; USGS Afrikaans water-cycle pages ('Die Hidrologiese Siklus') gave no readable labels; dictionary sources (interglot, DBNL) give 'invloei' only its general sense of flowing in (inflow) - into a dam, a river, the ground or the sea. English search for the same stage returns 'runoff', not 'inflow'. No source found that uses 'invloei' as the NAME of the land-to-sea stage.
items.fout: The process described (water running off the land back to the sea) is real. What cannot be settled is whether 'invloei' means it: the word's ordinary sense is any inflow, and Afrikaans references found call this stage 'afloop' / 'terugvloei'. A learner who later meets 'invloei in die dam' has been taught a narrower meaning. A person should decide whether the term stays (e.g. if it is the video's word) or changes.

items.bewering: Lopende water wat kleiner as 'n rivier is.
items.bron: WEET, 'Rivierstelsel' (weet.co.za/skoolwerk/rivierstelsel): 'klein stroompies wat spruite en later riviere word' and ''n Kleiner stroom of spruit wat later by 'n rivier aansluit' - Afrikaans reference usage of 'stroom' for flowing water smaller than a river. NOTE: Afrikaans 'stroom' also means a current or flow in general (af.wiktionary 'stroom'), and in Dutch can mean a large river; the sense given is one valid sense.

items.bewering: 'n Plek waar die grond vir lang tye nat bly.
items.bron: National Water Act 36 of 1998, s1 'wetland': land transitional between terrestrial and aquatic systems where the water table is usually at or near the surface, or which is periodically covered with shallow water, supporting vegetation adapted to saturated soil (acts.co.za). The plants are omitted; true at Grade 4.

items.bewering: Water wat in klein gaatjies en krake onder die grond sit.
items.bron: USGS ('groundwater pore spaces', usgs.gov/media/images/groundwater-pore-spaces): groundwater is stored underground in pore spaces and fractures; most is in tiny spaces between grains or narrow fractures in bedrock, not in underground lakes. Strictly, soil moisture above the water table is not groundwater; acceptable simplification.

items.bewering: Om iets soos water te stoor sodat dit later gebruik kan word.
items.bron: WEET, 'Damme van Suid-Afrika': 'Ongeveer die helfte van Suid-Afrika se reënval word in damme opgegaar' and ''n plek waar water opgegaar word' - usage matches 'store for later use'. A WAT/HAT entry could not be reached through search (tried 'opgaar betekenis bymekaarmaak bewaar stoor'); passed on usage evidence, as the meaning is not in doubt.

items.bewering: 'n Dam waar baie water gestoor word sodat mense dit later kan gebruik.
items.bron: WEET 'Damme van Suid-Afrika' and 'Gariepdam' (weet.co.za): the Gariep Dam is described as South Africa's largest storage dam; dams store about half the country's rainfall for later use.

items.bewering: 'n Plek waar water skoongemaak word sodat dit veilig is om te drink.
items.bron: Western Cape Government, opening of the Meulwater Treatment Works (gov.za speech; westerncape.gov.za): municipal water is purified so it is clean and safe to drink; Oudtshoorn Courant 2019-09-03, 'nuwe watersuiweringsaanleg by Kango Grotte'. NOTE (term, not fact): South African Afrikaans sources found say 'watersuiweringsaanleg' or '-werke'; 'watersuiweringsentrum' was not found in use, and the set pairs it with 'rioolwatersuiweringsaanleg', so the two plants get different head nouns. For the language check / a person, not a truth fault.

items.bewering: 'n Plek waar vuil rioolwater skoongemaak word voordat dit na riviere of ander waterbronne teruggaan.
items.bron: DWS Green Drop reporting and coverage (GroundUp 'Half of South Africa's sewage treatment works are failing'; Daily Maverick 2023-06-26, Johannesburg wastewater works): municipal wastewater works treat sewage and discharge the treated effluent into rivers (e.g. the Crocodile River) and the sea. The entry states the purpose; that many works currently fail is not a definitional matter.

items.bewering: 'n Openbare kraan in die straat of op oop grond wat baie gesinne van 'n gemeenskap deel.
items.bron: DWS reply to parliamentary question NW4169 (pmg.org.za/committee-question/40075): interim/basic service through communal standpipes within 200 m walking distance; DWAF 2004 design guidelines (via Haarhoff 2009, ircwash.org): standpipes shared by households, maximum 200 m from the home.

items.bewering: 'n Lang tyd waarin baie minder reën as gewoonlik op 'n plek val.
items.bron: NOAA / National Weather Service drought fact sheet (weather.gov/media/climateservices/Drought.pdf): a deficiency in precipitation over an extended period, usually a season or more; 'a period of abnormally dry weather'. 'Minder as gewoonlik' correctly makes it relative to the place's normal.

items.bewering: Om gewasse van die land af te haal wanneer hulle gereed is, en ook die gewasse wat so ingesamel word.
items.bron: Dictionary.com / Britannica Dictionary 'harvest': the gathering of ripe crops; also the crops gathered from a field (noun). Both senses given are correct; 'land' is the Afrikaans farm sense (field).

items.bewering: Iets wat mense gebruik en wat van plante of diere kom of deur mense gemaak word.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries 'product': a thing that is grown or produced, usually for sale. 'Van plante of diere kom' maps to grown, 'deur mense gemaak' to produced. NOTE: a raw mined product (coal, a diamond) is neither, so the entry is narrower than the word; harmless in the farming context of these lessons.

items.term: STEL: dam / opgaardam / reservoir / meer / opgaar
items.bewering: Read together: dam = water behind a man-made wall; opgaardam = a dam storing a lot of water for later; reservoir = a tank of clean water before distribution; meer = natural water surrounded by land; opgaar = store for later use.
items.bron: No contradiction between the five. By the 'opgaar' entry every dam is storing water for later, so 'dam' and 'opgaardam' differ only in 'baie' - redundant, not false. Reservoir is kept distinct from opgaardam by the South African municipal sense (see reservoir). The one fault in this cluster is meer's 'vanself gevorm' (see that item), which is what makes the meer/dam contrast absolute.

items.bewering: varswater gives 'die water in ... mere' as fresh; meer does not mention salt.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Lake': closed lakes are typically saline. Together the two entries let a learner infer that all lakes are fresh; neither entry says so, and 'soos' marks examples, so not counted as a fault - but whoever fixes 'meer' should know the two are read together.

items.term: STEL: varswater / watersiklus / verdamping / waterdamp / invloei
items.bewering: Evaporation turns water into invisible vapour that rises; the cycle evaporates, forms clouds, rains and flows away; invloei is water flowing back to the sea.
items.bron: USGS water-cycle material and NASA 'How do clouds form?': consistent - nothing in the set calls clouds 'waterdamp' (which is invisible), and no entry says the cycle starts at the sea. The only open point is the word 'invloei' itself (onseker item); 'watersiklus' says 'wegvloei' for the same step, so the set uses two different words for one stage.

items.bewering: A borehole is drilled down to underground water; underground water sits in small holes and cracks.
items.bron: USGS groundwater pore spaces; DWS groundwater report. Consistent, and together they avoid the underground-lake misconception.

items.bewering: A map is a reduced drawing from above; a plan view is how something looks from directly above; a key explains a map's symbols; a grid reference names one block by letter and number.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Map'. Consistent: kaart is a drawing made in plan view, planaansig is the view itself, sleutel and ruitverwysing are parts of a map.

items.bewering: Seven continents, five oceans around them, an island is land surrounded by water and smaller than the smallest continent.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Island'; New World Encyclopedia 'Continents'; NOAA/NGS on five oceans. Consistent: the eiland entry is what stops Australia (also surrounded by water) counting as an island, and Greenland (largest island) is under a third of Australia.

items.term: STEL: boerdery / veeboerdery / gewasse / oes / produk
items.bewering: Farming grows plants and keeps animals; livestock farming keeps animals for products; crops are plants grown for food and products; harvest gathers crops; a product comes from plants or animals or is made.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's 'farming' ('keeping animals OR growing plants'). Consistent, with one reading risk: if 'boerdery' is read as requiring both plants and animals, 'veeboerdery' (animals) would not be a kind of 'boerdery'. Noted on the boerdery item; not counted as a fault.

opsomming: Of 37 entries 35 are confirmed, 'meer' is contradicted because it makes natural origin part of what a lake is when man-made lakes such as Karibameer are lakes, and 'invloei' is uncertain because no source uses that word for the land-to-sea stage of the water cycle and its ordinary meaning is any inflow, so a person must decide the word before the writer touches 'meer'.
